chapter: Herbie Harper and Rasch's notes on Johnson
title: His mother as the one he could tell anything
summary: His mother always let him talk things out, and he learned to listen the same way.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I loved it when he talked about his mother. The time he spoke most freely of her was without the tape, and I have my notes on that meeting. "My mother did it all for me," he said, "the one closest to me. I could go to her with anything. I didn't give a hoot. I would tell her everything. She would always know how to deal with it. I'd be so happy just after talking about a situation that affected me, I'd go on and on and feel better." She just sat and let me talk and talk and talk. 'Well,' she'd say, 'you'll work it out.' I wasn't any closer to the solution than when I began talking, but I felt better. And, darn, I did work it out."
What is interesting about this is that J. C. was able to lend an ear to a lot of people and listen to them and let them talk themselves out.
